title: Fix Python effect fallback and greedy import prefix resolution
description:
Two high-severity findings from Codex adversarial review of sutra/188 + sutra/189:

1. **Effect fallback misses real Python attribute calls** (attributes.rs:155-162). The unresolved-ref fallback matches effect prefixes (e.g. `requests`, `subprocess`) against `RefRow.unresolved_name`, but the Python parser records attribute calls as bare identifiers — for `requests.get()`, the call ref stores `get`, not `requests.get`. The tests pass because they synthesize dotted RefRows that don't match production parser output. Fix: either emit full dotted callee chains from the Python parser for attribute calls, or reconstruct them before effect enrichment. Add an integration test that parses real Python source containing `requests.get()` and `subprocess.run()` and verifies convention attributes.

2. **Greedy prefix resolution creates false dependency edges** (python_imports.rs:160-175). `try_resolve_segments` walks shorter prefixes — `import pkg.foo.bar` resolves to `pkg/foo.py` even when `pkg/foo` isn't a package (no `__init__.py`). This can turn external/invalid imports into local dependency edges, corrupting graph/impact/constraint results. Fix: for the shorter-prefix fallback, verify the candidate is actually a package (has `__init__.py`) before accepting the match. Add regression test for `import pkg.foo.bar` with only `pkg/foo.py` present (should stay unresolved)."

acceptance_criteria.text: Effect enrichment fires for unresolved Python attribute calls like requests.get(), subprocess.run() when parsed from real Python source (integration test, not synthetic RefRows)
try_resolve_segments does not resolve import pkg.foo.bar to pkg/foo.py when pkg/foo is not a package (no __init__.py)
Regression test: import pkg.foo.bar with only pkg/foo.py present stays unresolved
Integration test: parse Python source with requests.get() and subprocess.run(), verify effect:net and effect:process attributes are tagged

execution_record:
Both fixes implemented in one commit. No divergence from plan.

Finding 1 (dotted chain refs): Added `build_dotted_call_chain` to Python parser's `walk_refs_recursive` — when an identifier is classified as a Call ref and is the attribute field of a nested `attribute` node, walks up collecting segments to emit an additional ref like `requests.get`. Simple call refs like `foo()` don't emit a chain.

Finding 2 (import kind): Added `kind` column to imports table (migration 0042), `kind` field to `ExtractedImport`/`InsertImportParams`/`ImportRow`. Python parser tags `collect_import_names` as `import`, `collect_import_from` as `from_import`. Other language parsers default to `import`. Resolver uses `try_resolve_strict` (full-path only) for plain imports and existing `try_resolve_segments` (greedy prefix fallback) for from-imports.

Also included the nondeterministic root ordering fix (sort discovered roots) from the earlier medium finding."
